source.title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds

accepted.question_text: Let G be a group and let M and N be closed aspherical manifolds whose fundamental groups are both isomorphic to G. Must M and N be homeomorphic, and must every homotopy equivalence M -> N be homotopic to a homeomorphism?

evidence.quote: If M and N are aspherical closed manifolds with π1(M) ∼= π1(N) ∼= G, then M and N are homeomorphic and any homotopy equivalence M → N is homotopic to a homeomorphism.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a torsionfree group. Is it true that the negative algebraic K-groups Kn(ZG) vanish for all n <= -1, that the reduced projective class group K̃0(ZG) vanishes, that the Whitehead group Wh(G) vanishes, and that for every homomorphism w: G -> {±1} the w-twisted L-theoretic assembly map Hn(BG; wL⟨−∞⟩) -> L⟨−∞⟩n(RG,w) is bijective?

For a natural number n, is a finitely presented group an n-dimensional Poincaré duality group exactly when it occurs as the fundamental group of an aspherical closed n-dimensional topological manifold?
accepted.context_brief: Poincaré duality groups and manifold realization

evidence.quote: A finitely presented group is a n-dimensional Poincare duality group if and only if it is the fundamental group of an aspherical closed n-dimensional topological manifold.

accepted.question_text: Suppose X is an aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold that has the disjoint disks property (DDP). Must X be homotopy equivalent to a closed manifold?
accepted.context_brief: Resolution obstruction in the aspherical case

evidence.quote: Is every aspherical compact homology ANR-manifold having the DDP homotopy equivalent to a closed manifold?

accepted.question_text: Let M be an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group has non-trivial center. Does M admit a finite covering space with a non-trivial S1-action?

evidence.quote: If M is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group has a non-trivial center, is there a finite covering which admits a non-trivial S1-action?

accepted.question_text: Let f: M -> N be a map between aspherical closed manifolds that induces a surjection on fundamental groups. Under what conditions is f homotopy equivalent either to the projection map of a locally trivial topological fiber bundle or to a manifold approximate fibration?

evidence.quote:
Let f : M → N be a map of aspherical closed manifolds which induces a surjection on fundamental groups.
Under which conditions is it homotopy equivalent to the projection of a locally trivial topological fiber bundle (or to a Manifold Approximate Fibration)?

accepted.question_text: If M is an aspherical closed manifold of even dimension, must its Euler characteristic satisfy (-1)^(dim(M)/2) * χ(M) >= 0? More generally, if M is a closed Riemannian manifold of even dimension, must one have (-1)^(dim(M)/2) * χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) < 0, (-1)^(dim(M)/2) * χ(M) >= 0 when sec(M) <= 0, χ(M) >= 0 when sec(M) >= 0, and χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) > 0?
accepted.context_brief: Hopf conjecture on Euler characteristic and curvature

accepted.question_text: If M is an aspherical closed manifold, must every L²-Betti number b_p^(2)(M̃) vanish outside the middle dimension, meaning b_p^(2)(M̃) = 0 whenever 2p != dim(M)? In the negatively curved Riemannian case, must the middle-dimensional L²-Betti number additionally be strictly positive when 2p = dim(M)?

evidence.quote:
If M is an aspherical closed manifold, then
b(2)p(M̃) = 0 if 2p ≠ dim(M).

If M is a closed connected Riemannian manifold with negative sectional curvature, then
b(2)p(M̃)
= 0 if 2p ≠ dim(M);
> 0 if 2p = dim(M).

accepted.question_text: If M is an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension, must its universal cover M̃ be det-L²-acyclic and satisfy (-1)^((dim(M)-1)/2) * ρ^(2)(M̃) >= 0? If M is a closed connected Riemannian manifold of odd dimension with negative sectional curvature, must the same quantity be strictly positive? If M is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, must M̃ be det-L²-acyclic and satisfy ρ^(2)(M̃) = 0?

evidence.quote:
If M is an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension, then M̃ is det-L2-acyclic and
(−1)(dim(M)−1)/2 · ρ(2)(M̃) ≥ 0.

If M is a closed connected Riemannian manifold of odd dimension with negative sectional curvature, then M̃ is det-L2-acyclic and
(−1)(dim(M)−1)/2 · ρ(2)(M̃) > 0.

If M is an aspherical closed manifold whose fundamental group contains an amenable infinite normal subgroup, then M̃ is det-L2-acyclic and
ρ(2)(M̃) = 0.

accepted.question_text: Let M be an aspherical closed orientable manifold with vanishing simplicial volume ||M|| = 0. Must its universal cover M̃ be of determinant class, and must all of its L²-Betti numbers vanish while its L²-torsion also vanishes; that is, b_p^(2)(M̃) = 0 for all p >= 0 and ρ^(2)(M̃) = 0?

Let M̃ be the universal covering of an aspherical closed Riemannian manifold M, equipped with the lifted Riemannian metric. Must zero belong to the spectrum of the minimal closure of the Laplacian on square-integrable smooth p-forms on M̃ for at least one degree p >= 0?
accepted.context_brief: Zero in the spectrum for universal covers

evidence.quote:
Let M̃ be a complete Riemannian manifold. Suppose that M̃ is the universal covering of an aspherical closed Riemannian manifold M (with the Riemannian metric coming from M). Then for some p ≥ 0 zero is in the Spectrum of the minimal closure
(∆p)min : dom((∆p)min) ⊂ L2Ωp(M̃) → L2Ωp(M̃)
of the Laplacian acting on smooth p-forms on M̃.

accepted.question_text: Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of dimension d with fundamental group G = π1(M), and let G = G0 ⊇ G1 ⊇ ... be a descending chain of normal subgroups of finite index with trivial intersection. Writing M[i] = Gi\M̃ for the covering corresponding to Gi and letting F be a field, do the normalized Betti numbers b_n(M[i];F) / [G : Gi] converge to the L²-Betti numbers b_p^(2)(M̃) for every p >= 0? Moreover, if 2p+1 != d, must the normalized logarithms ln(|tors(Hp(M[i]))|) / [G : Gi] converge to 0, and if d = 2p+1, must they converge to (-1)^p * ρ^(2)(M̃)?
accepted.context_brief: Homological growth in towers of finite covers

evidence.quote:
Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of dimension d and fundamental group G = π1(M). Let G = G0 ⊇ G1 ⊇ ··· be a descending sequence of in G normal subgroups [G : Gi] with trivial intersection ⋂i≥0 Gi = {1}. Put M[i] = Gi\M̃, where M̃ is the universal covering. Let F be an field. Then
1. We get for any p ≥ 0
b(2)p(M̃) = limi→∞ bn(M[i];F) / [G : Gi];

2. We get for any natural number p with 2p+1 ≠ d
limi→∞ ln(|tors(Hp(M[i]))|) / [G : Gi] = 0,
and we get in the case d = 2p+1
limi→∞ ln(|tors(Hn(M[i]))|) / [G : Gi] = (−1)p · ρ(2)(M̃).

accepted.question_text: Can an aspherical closed smooth manifold admit a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature, or does every such manifold necessarily fail to admit one?
accepted.context_brief: Positive scalar curvature on aspherical manifolds

evidence.quote: An aspherical closed smooth manifold does not admit a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.

accepted.question_text: If one considers a random closed smooth manifold in the informal sense discussed by the paper, should one expect it to admit a Riemannian metric with non-positive sectional curvature?

evidence.quote: A related question would be whether a random closed smooth manifold admits a Riemannian metric with non-positive sectional curvature.
